e-3455.knowledge_point: Simplifying an Expression Using the Alternate Forms of the Secant-Tangent Identity
e-3455.worked_solution:
First, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

$$
\begin{aligned} & (1) & 1+{tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & (2) & {tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta -1 \\  & (3) & {sec}^{2}⁡\theta -{tan}^{2}⁡\theta =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can rewrite our expression using $(3),$ as follows:

$$
\dfrac{1}{\color{blue}\sec^2 \theta - \tan^2 \theta} =  \dfrac{1}{\color{blue} 1} = 1
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\dfrac{1}{\sec^2 \theta - \tan^2 \theta} = 1.
$$

e-3463.knowledge_point: Simplifying an Expression by Factoring Alternative Forms of the Secant-Tangent Identity
e-3463.worked_solution:
First, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

$$
\begin{aligned} & (1) & 1+{tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & (2) & {tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta -1 \\  & (3) & {sec}^{2}⁡\theta -{tan}^{2}⁡\theta =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can rewrite our expression using $(3),$ as follows:

$$
\dfrac{\color{blue}1}{\sec{\theta}+\tan{\theta}} = \dfrac{\color{blue}\sec^2{\theta} - \tan^2{\theta}}{\sec{\theta} + \tan{\theta}}
$$

Next, we can further simplify our expression by factoring the numerator as a difference of squares, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡\theta -{tan}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta +\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta } & =\frac{(\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta -\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta )(\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta +\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta )}{\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta +\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{(\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta -\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta )\cancel{(\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta +\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta )}}{\cancel{(\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta +\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta )}} \\  & =\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta -\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\dfrac{1}{\sec\theta + \tan\theta} =  \sec{\theta} - \tan{\theta}.
$$

e-3144.problem: Express $\tan^2 x\sec^2 x - \tan^4 x +1$ in terms of $\sec x$ only.
e-3144.worked_solution:
First, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

$$
\begin{aligned} & (1) & 1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x \\  & (2) & {tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x-1 \\  & (3) & {sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x=1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can rewrite our expression using $(3),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{tan}^{2}⁡x{sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{4}⁡x+1 & ={tan}^{2}⁡x({sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x)+1 \\  & ={tan}^{2}⁡x\cdot (1)+1 \\  & ={tan}^{2}⁡x+1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can use $(1),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{tan}^{2}⁡x+1 & ={sec}^{2}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\tan^2 x\sec^2 x - \tan^4 x +1 = \sec^2 x.
$$

after.worked_solution:
First, we expand the parentheses:

$$
(\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta -1)(\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta +1)={sec}^{2}⁡\theta -1
$$

Then, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

$$
\begin{aligned} & (1) & 1+{tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & (2) & {tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta -1 \\  & (3) & {sec}^{2}⁡\theta -{tan}^{2}⁡\theta =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can rewrite our expression using $(2),$ as follows:

$$
{sec}^{2}⁡\theta -1={tan}^{2}⁡\theta 
$$

$$
(\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta -1)(\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta +1)={tan}^{2}⁡\theta .
$$

decision.explanation: By the difference of squares, (sec x−tan x)(sec x+tan x)=sec² x−tan² x=1 using the secant–tangent identity.

after.name: Question 2
after.worked_solution:
First, we expand the parentheses:

$$
(\operatorname{sec}⁡x-\operatorname{tan}⁡x)(\operatorname{sec}⁡x+\operatorname{tan}⁡x)={sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x
$$

Then, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

$$
\begin{aligned} & (1) & 1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x \\  & (2) & {tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x-1 \\  & (3) & {sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x=1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can rewrite our expression using $(3),$ as follows:

$$
{sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x=1
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
(\operatorname{sec}⁡x-\operatorname{tan}⁡x)(\operatorname{sec}⁡x+\operatorname{tan}⁡x)=1.
$$

after.name: Question 3
after.worked_solution:
First, we recall the following identities: 

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\,\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\,\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }
$$

Next, we expand the parentheses and use the above identities, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{csc}^{2}⁡\theta ({tan}^{2}⁡\theta -{sin}^{2}⁡\theta ) & ={csc}^{2}⁡\theta \cdot {tan}^{2}⁡\theta -{csc}^{2}⁡\theta \cdot {sin}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\cdot \frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }-\frac{1}{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\cdot {sin}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{\cancel{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }}\cdot \frac{\cancel{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }}{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }-\frac{1}{\cancel{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }}\cdot \cancel{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }-1 \\  & ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta -1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

$$
\begin{aligned} & (1) & 1+{tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & (2) & {tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta -1 \\  & (3) & {sec}^{2}⁡\theta -{tan}^{2}⁡\theta =1\end{aligned}
$$

We can rewrite our expression using $(2),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{sec}^{2}⁡\theta -1 & ={tan}^{2}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
{csc}^{2}⁡\theta ({tan}^{2}⁡\theta -{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )={tan}^{2}⁡\theta .
$$

Question 3

csc2⁡θ(tan2⁡θ−sin2⁡θ)=

a
tan2⁡θ
b
tan2⁡θ−1
c
1−tan2⁡θ
d
tan⁡θ
e
tan2⁡θ+1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we recall the following identities:

tan⁡θ=sin⁡θcos⁡θsec⁡θ=1cos⁡θcsc⁡θ=1sin⁡θ

Next, we expand the parentheses and use the above identities, as follows:

csc2⁡θ(tan2⁡θ−sin2⁡θ)=csc2⁡θ⋅tan2⁡θ−csc2⁡θ⋅sin2⁡θ=1sin2⁡θ⋅sin2⁡θcos2⁡θ−1sin2⁡θ⋅sin2⁡θ=1sin2⁡θ⋅sin2⁡θcos2⁡θ−1sin2⁡θ⋅sin2⁡θ=1cos2⁡θ−1=sec2⁡θ−1

Finally, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

(1)1+tan2⁡θ=sec2⁡θ(2)tan2⁡θ=sec2⁡θ−1(3)sec2⁡θ−tan2⁡θ=1

We can rewrite our expression using (2), as follows: sec2⁡θ−1=tan2⁡θ

Therefore, we conclude that

csc2⁡θ(tan2⁡θ−sin2⁡θ)=tan2⁡θ.

content.knowledge_point: Simplifying an Expression Using the Alternate Forms of the Secant-Tangent Identity
content.worked_solution:
First, we recall the following identities: 

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\,\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\,\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }
$$

Next, we expand the parentheses and use the above identities, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{csc}^{2}⁡\theta ({tan}^{2}⁡\theta -{sin}^{2}⁡\theta ) & ={csc}^{2}⁡\theta \cdot {tan}^{2}⁡\theta -{csc}^{2}⁡\theta \cdot {sin}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\cdot \frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }-\frac{1}{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\cdot {sin}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{\cancel{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }}\cdot \frac{\cancel{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }}{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }-\frac{1}{\cancel{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }}\cdot \cancel{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }-1 \\  & ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta -1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

$$
\begin{aligned} & (1) & 1+{tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & (2) & {tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta -1 \\  & (3) & {sec}^{2}⁡\theta -{tan}^{2}⁡\theta =1\end{aligned}
$$

We can rewrite our expression using $(2),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{sec}^{2}⁡\theta -1 & ={tan}^{2}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
{csc}^{2}⁡\theta ({tan}^{2}⁡\theta -{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )={tan}^{2}⁡\theta .
$$

after.name: Question 4
after.worked_solution:
First, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

$$
\begin{aligned} & (1) & 1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x \\  & (2) & {tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x-1 \\  & (3) & {sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x=1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can rewrite our expression using $(2),$ as follows:

$$
\frac{{tan}^{2}⁡x}{{sec}^{2}⁡x}-1+{sin}^{2}⁡x=\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x-1}{{sec}^{2}⁡x}-1+{sin}^{2}⁡x
$$

Next, we recall the following identity: 

$$
1-{sin}^{2}⁡x={cos}^{2}⁡x
$$

Using the above identity, we can further simplify our expression as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x-1}{{sec}^{2}⁡x}-1+{sin}^{2}⁡x & =\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x-1}{{sec}^{2}⁡x}-(1-{sin}^{2}⁡x) \\  & =\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x-1}{{sec}^{2}⁡x}-{cos}^{2}⁡x \\  & =\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x}{{sec}^{2}⁡x}-\frac{1}{{sec}^{2}⁡x}-{cos}^{2}⁡x \\  & =\frac{\cancel{{sec}^{2}⁡x}}{\cancel{{sec}^{2}⁡x}}-\frac{1}{{sec}^{2}⁡x}-{cos}^{2}⁡x \\  & =1-\frac{1}{{sec}^{2}⁡x}-{cos}^{2}⁡x \\  & =1-{cos}^{2}⁡x-{cos}^{2}⁡x \\  & =1-2{cos}^{2}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{{tan}^{2}⁡x}{{sec}^{2}⁡x}-1+{sin}^{2}⁡x=1-2{cos}^{2}⁡x.
$$

content.knowledge_point: Simplifying an Expression Using the Alternate Forms of the Secant-Tangent Identity
content.worked_solution:
First, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

$$
\begin{aligned} & (1) & 1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x \\  & (2) & {tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x-1 \\  & (3) & {sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x=1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can rewrite our expression using $(2),$ as follows:

$$
\frac{{tan}^{2}⁡x}{{sec}^{2}⁡x}-1+{sin}^{2}⁡x=\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x-1}{{sec}^{2}⁡x}-1+{sin}^{2}⁡x
$$

Next, we recall the following identity: 

$$
1-{sin}^{2}⁡x={cos}^{2}⁡x
$$

Using the above identity, we can further simplify our expression as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x-1}{{sec}^{2}⁡x}-1+{sin}^{2}⁡x & =\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x-1}{{sec}^{2}⁡x}-(1-{sin}^{2}⁡x) \\  & =\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x-1}{{sec}^{2}⁡x}-{cos}^{2}⁡x \\  & =\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x}{{sec}^{2}⁡x}-\frac{1}{{sec}^{2}⁡x}-{cos}^{2}⁡x \\  & =\frac{\cancel{{sec}^{2}⁡x}}{\cancel{{sec}^{2}⁡x}}-\frac{1}{{sec}^{2}⁡x}-{cos}^{2}⁡x \\  & =1-\frac{1}{{sec}^{2}⁡x}-{cos}^{2}⁡x \\  & =1-{cos}^{2}⁡x-{cos}^{2}⁡x \\  & =1-2{cos}^{2}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{{tan}^{2}⁡x}{{sec}^{2}⁡x}-1+{sin}^{2}⁡x=1-2{cos}^{2}⁡x.
$$

after.name: Question 5
after.worked_solution:
First, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

$$
\begin{aligned} & (1) & 1+{tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & (2) & {tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta -1 \\  & (3) & {sec}^{2}⁡\theta -{tan}^{2}⁡\theta =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can rewrite our expression using $(2),$ as follows:

$$
\frac{{tan}^{3}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{csc}⁡\theta }{{sec}^{2}⁡\theta -1}=\frac{{tan}^{3}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{csc}⁡\theta }{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta }
$$

Next, we recall the following identity: 

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }
$$

Using the above identity, we can further simplify our expression as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{tan}^{3}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{csc}⁡\theta }{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta } & =\frac{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{csc}⁡\theta }{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\cancel{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta }\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{csc}⁡\theta }{\cancel{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta }} \\  & =\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{csc}⁡\theta  \\  & =\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }}{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\cdot \frac{1}{\cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }} \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta } \\  & =\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{{tan}^{3}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{csc}⁡\theta }{{sec}^{2}⁡\theta -1}=\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta .
$$

EXPLANATION

First, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

(1)1+tan2⁡θ=sec2⁡θ(2)tan2⁡θ=sec2⁡θ−1(3)sec2⁡θ−tan2⁡θ=1

Therefore, we can rewrite our expression using (2), as follows:

tan3⁡θ⋅csc⁡θsec2⁡θ−1=tan3⁡θ⋅csc⁡θtan2⁡θ

Next, we recall the following identity:

tan⁡θ=sin⁡θcos⁡θ

Using the above identity, we can further simplify our expression as follows:

tan3⁡θ⋅csc⁡θtan2⁡θ=tan2⁡θ⋅tan⁡θ⋅csc⁡θtan2⁡θ=tan2⁡θ⋅tan⁡θ⋅csc⁡θtan2⁡θ=tan⁡θ⋅csc⁡θ=tan⁡θ⋅1sin⁡θ=sin⁡θcos⁡θ⋅1sin⁡θ=sin⁡θcos⁡θ⋅1sin⁡θ=1cos⁡θ=sec⁡θ

Therefore, we conclude that

tan3⁡θ⋅csc⁡θsec2⁡θ−1=sec⁡θ.

content.knowledge_point: Simplifying an Expression Using the Alternate Forms of the Secant-Tangent Identity
content.worked_solution:
First, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

$$
\begin{aligned} & (1) & 1+{tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & (2) & {tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta -1 \\  & (3) & {sec}^{2}⁡\theta -{tan}^{2}⁡\theta =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can rewrite our expression using $(2),$ as follows:

$$
\frac{{tan}^{3}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{csc}⁡\theta }{{sec}^{2}⁡\theta -1}=\frac{{tan}^{3}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{csc}⁡\theta }{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta }
$$

Next, we recall the following identity: 

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }
$$

Using the above identity, we can further simplify our expression as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{tan}^{3}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{csc}⁡\theta }{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta } & =\frac{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{csc}⁡\theta }{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\cancel{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta }\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{csc}⁡\theta }{\cancel{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta }} \\  & =\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{csc}⁡\theta  \\  & =\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }}{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\cdot \frac{1}{\cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }} \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta } \\  & =\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{{tan}^{3}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{csc}⁡\theta }{{sec}^{2}⁡\theta -1}=\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta .
$$

after.name: Question 6
after.worked_solution:
First, we can simplify our expression by factoring it, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{sec}^{4}⁡x-2{sec}^{2}⁡x\cdot {tan}^{2}⁡x+{tan}^{4}⁡x & =({sec}^{2}⁡x)^{2}-2{sec}^{2}⁡x\cdot {tan}^{2}⁡x+({tan}^{2}⁡x)^{2} \\  & ={({sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x)}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

$$
\begin{aligned} & (1) & 1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x \\  & (2) & {tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x-1 \\  & (3) & {sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x=1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can rewrite our expression using $(3),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{({sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x)}^{2} & ={(1)}^{2} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
{sec}^{4}⁡x-2{sec}^{2}⁡x\cdot {tan}^{2}⁡x+{tan}^{4}⁡x=1.
$$

after.name: Question 7
after.worked_solution:
First, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

$$
\begin{aligned} & (1) & 1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x \\  & (2) & {tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x-1 \\  & (3) & {sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x=1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can rewrite our expression using $(2),$ as follows:

$$
\frac{{tan}^{2}⁡x}{{sec}^{2}⁡x-2\operatorname{sec}⁡x+1}=\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x-1}{{sec}^{2}⁡x-2\operatorname{sec}⁡x+1}
$$

Next, we can further simplify our expression by factoring it as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x-1}{(\operatorname{sec}⁡x-1)^{2}} & =\frac{(\operatorname{sec}⁡x-1)(\operatorname{sec}⁡x+1)}{(\operatorname{sec}⁡x-1)(\operatorname{sec}⁡x-1)} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{(\operatorname{sec}⁡x-1)}(\operatorname{sec}⁡x+1)}{\cancel{(\operatorname{sec}⁡x-1)}(\operatorname{sec}⁡x-1)} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{sec}⁡x+1}{\operatorname{sec}⁡x-1}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{{tan}^{2}⁡x}{{sec}^{2}⁡x-2\operatorname{sec}⁡x+1}=\frac{\operatorname{sec}⁡x+1}{\operatorname{sec}⁡x-1}.
$$

after.worked_solution:
First, we recall the following identities: 

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\,\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\,\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }
$$

Using the above identity, we can simplify our expression as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{csc}^{2}⁡\theta {tan}^{4}⁡\theta -{sec}^{2}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡\theta  & =\frac{1}{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\frac{{sin}^{4}⁡\theta }{{cos}^{4}⁡\theta }-\frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{sin}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \cdot {sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{{cos}^{4}⁡\theta }-\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{1}{\cancel{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }}\frac{\cancel{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\cdot {sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{{cos}^{4}⁡\theta }-\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }-\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta {tan}^{2}⁡\theta -{tan}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & ={tan}^{2}⁡\theta ({sec}^{2}⁡\theta -1)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

$$
\begin{aligned} & (1) & 1+{tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & (2) & {tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta -1 \\  & (3) & {sec}^{2}⁡\theta -{tan}^{2}⁡\theta =1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can rewrite our expression using $(2),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{tan}^{2}⁡\theta ({sec}^{2}⁡\theta -1) & ={tan}^{2}⁡\theta \cdot {tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={tan}^{4}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
{csc}^{2}⁡\theta {tan}^{4}⁡\theta -{sec}^{2}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡\theta ={tan}^{4}⁡\theta .
$$

decision.explanation: Factor tan² x=sec² x−1=(sec x−1)(sec x+1). Dividing by sec x+1 gives sec x−1, and subtracting 1 gives sec x−2.

after.name: Question 9
after.worked_solution:
First, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

$$
\begin{aligned} & (1) & 1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x \\  & (2) & {tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x-1 \\  & (3) & {sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x=1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can rewrite our expression using $(2),$ as follows:

$$
\frac{{tan}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{sec}⁡x+1}-1=\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x-1}{\operatorname{sec}⁡x+1}-1
$$

Finally, we can further simplify our expression by factoring the numerator as a difference of squares, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x-1}{\operatorname{sec}⁡x+1}-1 & =\frac{(\operatorname{sec}⁡x+1)(\operatorname{sec}⁡x-1)}{\operatorname{sec}⁡x+1}-1 \\  & =\frac{\cancel{(\operatorname{sec}⁡x+1)}(\operatorname{sec}⁡x-1)}{\cancel{\operatorname{sec}⁡x+1}}-1 \\  & =\operatorname{sec}⁡x-1-1 \\  & =\operatorname{sec}⁡x-2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{{tan}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{sec}⁡x+1}-1=\operatorname{sec}⁡x-2.
$$

EXPLANATION

First, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

(1)1+tan2⁡x=sec2⁡x(2)tan2⁡x=sec2⁡x−1(3)sec2⁡x−tan2⁡x=1

Therefore, we can rewrite our expression using (2), as follows: tan2⁡xsec⁡x+1−1=sec2⁡x−1sec⁡x+1−1

Finally, we can further simplify our expression by factoring the numerator as a difference of squares, as follows:

sec2⁡x−1sec⁡x+1−1=(sec⁡x+1)(sec⁡x−1)sec⁡x+1−1=(sec⁡x+1)(sec⁡x−1)sec⁡x+1−1=sec⁡x−1−1=sec⁡x−2

Therefore, we conclude that

tan2⁡xsec⁡x+1−1=sec⁡x−2.

after.name: Question 10
after.worked_solution:
First, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

$$
\begin{aligned} & (1) & 1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x \\  & (2) & {tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x-1 \\  & (3) & {sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x=1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can rewrite our expression using $(3),$ as follows:

$$
\frac{1}{\operatorname{tan}⁡x-\operatorname{sec}⁡x}=\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{sec}⁡x-\operatorname{tan}⁡x}
$$

Now, we factor the numerator as a difference of squares, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{sec}⁡x-\operatorname{tan}⁡x} & =\frac{(\operatorname{sec}⁡x-\operatorname{tan}⁡x)(\operatorname{sec}⁡x+\operatorname{tan}⁡x)}{(\operatorname{sec}⁡x-\operatorname{tan}⁡x)} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{(\operatorname{sec}⁡x-\operatorname{tan}⁡x)}(\operatorname{sec}⁡x+\operatorname{tan}⁡x)}{\cancel{(\operatorname{sec}⁡x-\operatorname{tan}⁡x)}} \\  & =\operatorname{sec}⁡x+\operatorname{tan}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{1}{\operatorname{sec}⁡x-\operatorname{tan}⁡x}=\operatorname{sec}⁡x+\operatorname{tan}⁡x.
$$

EXPLANATION

First, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

(1)1+tan2⁡x=sec2⁡x(2)tan2⁡x=sec2⁡x−1(3)sec2⁡x−tan2⁡x=1

Therefore, we can rewrite our expression using (3), as follows:

1tan⁡x−sec⁡x=sec2⁡x−tan2⁡xsec⁡x−tan⁡x

Now, we factor the numerator as a difference of squares, and simplify: sec2⁡x−tan2⁡xsec⁡x−tan⁡x=(sec⁡x−tan⁡x)(sec⁡x+tan⁡x)(sec⁡x−tan⁡x)=(sec⁡x−tan⁡x)(sec⁡x+tan⁡x)(sec⁡x−tan⁡x)=sec⁡x+tan⁡x

Therefore, we conclude that

1sec⁡x−tan⁡x=sec⁡x+tan⁡x.

Which of the following is equivalent to tan2⁡xsec2⁡x−tan2⁡x−1?

a
1+tan4⁡x
b
tan2⁡x+tan4⁡x
c
tan4⁡x−1
d
tan2⁡x

1−tan2⁡x

decision.explanation: Factor the first two terms to obtain tan² x(sec² x−1)−1. Since sec² x−1=tan² x, this equals tan⁴ x−1.

after.name: Question 11
after.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${tan}^{2}⁡x{sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x-1?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

$$
\begin{aligned} & (1) & 1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x \\  & (2) & {tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x-1 \\  & (3) & {sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x=1\end{aligned}
$$

We can simplify our expression using $(2),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{tan}^{2}⁡x{sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x-1 & ={tan}^{2}⁡x({sec}^{2}⁡x-1)-1 \\  & ={tan}^{2}⁡x({tan}^{2}⁡x)-1 \\  & ={tan}^{4}⁡x-1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
{tan}^{2}⁡x{sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x-1={tan}^{4}⁡x-1.
$$

Question 11
?

Which of the following is equivalent to tan2⁡xsec2⁡x−tan2⁡x−1?

a
1+tan4⁡x
b
tan2⁡x+tan4⁡x
c
tan4⁡x−1
d
tan2⁡x
e
1−tan2⁡x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

(1)1+tan2⁡x=sec2⁡x(2)tan2⁡x=sec2⁡x−1(3)sec2⁡x−tan2⁡x=1

We can simplify our expression using (2), as follows:

tan2⁡xsec2⁡x−tan2⁡x−1=tan2⁡x(sec2⁡x−1)−1=tan2⁡x(tan2⁡x)−1=tan4⁡x−1

Therefore, we conclude that

tan2⁡xsec2⁡x−tan2⁡x−1=tan4⁡x−1.

after.name: Question 12
after.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to $\frac{1}{{tan}^{2}⁡x{sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{4}⁡x+1}?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

$$
\begin{aligned} & (1) & 1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x \\  & (2) & {tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x-1 \\  & (3) & {sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x=1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can rewrite our expression using $(3),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{{tan}^{2}⁡x{sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{4}⁡x+1} & =\frac{1}{{tan}^{2}⁡x({sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x)+1} \\  & =\frac{1}{{tan}^{2}⁡x\cdot 1+1} \\  & =\frac{1}{{tan}^{2}⁡x+1}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can use $(1),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{{tan}^{2}⁡x+1} & =\frac{1}{{sec}^{2}⁡x} \\  & ={(\frac{1}{\operatorname{sec}⁡x})}^{2} \\  & ={cos}^{2}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{1}{{tan}^{2}⁡x{sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{4}⁡x+1}={cos}^{2}⁡x.
$$

a

b
cos2⁡x
c
cos⁡x−1
d
cos⁡x+1
e
−cos2⁡x

Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

(1)1+tan2⁡x=sec2⁡x(2)tan2⁡x=sec2⁡x−1(3)sec2⁡x−tan2⁡x=1

Therefore, we can rewrite our expression using (3), as follows:

1tan2⁡xsec2⁡x−tan4⁡x+1=1tan2⁡x(sec2⁡x−tan2⁡x)+1=1tan2⁡x⋅1+1=1tan2⁡x+1

Finally, we can use (1), as follows:

1tan2⁡x+1=1sec2⁡x=(1sec⁡x)2=cos2⁡x

Therefore, we conclude that

1tan2⁡xsec2⁡x−tan4⁡x+1=cos2⁡x.

after.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to $\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x}{{sec}^{4}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x-1}?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

$$
\begin{aligned} & (1) & 1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x \\  & (2) & {tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x-1 \\  & (3) & {sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x=1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can rewrite our expression using $(1),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x}{{sec}^{4}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x-1} & =\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x}{{sec}^{4}⁡x-({tan}^{2}⁡x+1)} \\  & =\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x}{{sec}^{4}⁡x-{sec}^{2}⁡x}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can further simplify our expression, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x}{{sec}^{4}⁡x-{sec}^{2}⁡x} & =\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x}{{sec}^{2}⁡x({sec}^{2}⁡x-1)} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{{sec}^{2}⁡x}}{\cancel{{sec}^{2}⁡x}({sec}^{2}⁡x-1)} \\  & =\frac{1}{{sec}^{2}⁡x-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{(1+{tan}^{2}⁡x)-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{{tan}^{2}⁡x} \\  & ={(\frac{1}{\operatorname{tan}⁡x})}^{2} \\  & ={cot}^{2}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x}{{sec}^{4}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x-1}={cot}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Question 13

Which of the following is equivalent to sec2⁡xsec4⁡x−tan2⁡x−1?

a
cot2⁡x−1
b
1−cot⁡x
c
2cot⁡x
d
cot2⁡x
e
cot⁡x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

(1)1+tan2⁡x=sec2⁡x(2)tan2⁡x=sec2⁡x−1(3)sec2⁡x−tan2⁡x=1

Therefore, we can rewrite our expression using (1), as follows:

sec2⁡xsec4⁡x−tan2⁡x−1=sec2⁡xsec4⁡x−(tan2⁡x+1)=sec2⁡xsec4⁡x−sec2⁡x

Finally, we can further simplify our expression, as follows: sec2⁡xsec4⁡x−sec2⁡x=sec2⁡xsec2⁡x(sec2⁡x−1)=sec2⁡xsec2⁡x(sec2⁡x−1)=1sec2⁡x−1=1(1+tan2⁡x)−1=1tan2⁡x=(1tan⁡x)2=cot2⁡x

Therefore, we conclude that

sec2⁡xsec4⁡x−tan2⁡x−1=cot2⁡x.

$$
\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x}{{sec}^{4}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x-1}={cot}^{2}⁡x.

after.name: Question 14
after.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to $\frac{{tan}^{4}⁡\theta -{sec}^{2}⁡\theta +1}{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta }?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

$$
\begin{aligned} & (1) & 1+{tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & (2) & {tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta -1 \\  & (3) & {sec}^{2}⁡\theta -{tan}^{2}⁡\theta =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can rewrite our expression using $(2),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{tan}^{4}⁡\theta -{sec}^{2}⁡\theta +1}{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta } & =\frac{{tan}^{4}⁡\theta -({sec}^{2}⁡\theta -1)}{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{{tan}^{4}⁡\theta -{tan}^{2}⁡\theta }{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can further simplify our expression and use again $(2)$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{tan}^{4}⁡\theta -{tan}^{2}⁡\theta }{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta } & =\frac{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta ({tan}^{2}⁡\theta -1)}{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\cancel{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta }({tan}^{2}⁡\theta -1)}{\cancel{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta }} \\  & ={tan}^{2}⁡\theta -1 \\  & =({sec}^{2}⁡\theta -1)-1 \\  & ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta -2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{{tan}^{4}⁡\theta -{sec}^{2}⁡\theta +1}{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta }={sec}^{2}⁡\theta -2.
$$

Question 14

Which of the following is equivalent to tan4⁡θ−sec2⁡θ+1tan2⁡θ?

a
sec⁡θ+2
b
−sec2⁡θ
c
sec2⁡θ−2
d
1−sec⁡θ
e
sec⁡θ
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

(1)1+tan2⁡θ=sec2⁡θ(2)tan2⁡θ=sec2⁡θ−1(3)sec2⁡θ−tan2⁡θ=1

Therefore, we can rewrite our expression using (2), as follows:

tan4⁡θ−sec2⁡θ+1tan2⁡θ=tan4⁡θ−(sec2⁡θ−1)tan2⁡θ=tan4⁡θ−tan2⁡θtan2⁡θ

Finally, we can further simplify our expression and use again (2), as follows:

tan4⁡θ−tan2⁡θtan2⁡θ=tan2⁡θ(tan2⁡θ−1)tan2⁡θ=tan2⁡θ(tan2⁡θ−1)tan2⁡θ=tan2⁡θ−1=(sec2⁡θ−1)−1=sec2⁡θ−2

Therefore, we conclude that

tan4⁡θ−sec2⁡θ+1tan2⁡θ=sec2⁡θ−2.

content.knowledge_point: Simplifying an Expression by Factoring and Using Various Forms of the Secant-Tangent Identity
content.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to $\frac{{tan}^{4}⁡\theta -{sec}^{2}⁡\theta +1}{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta }?$
content.worked_solution:
First, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

$$
\begin{aligned} & (1) & 1+{tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & (2) & {tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta -1 \\  & (3) & {sec}^{2}⁡\theta -{tan}^{2}⁡\theta =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can rewrite our expression using $(2),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{tan}^{4}⁡\theta -{sec}^{2}⁡\theta +1}{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta } & =\frac{{tan}^{4}⁡\theta -({sec}^{2}⁡\theta -1)}{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{{tan}^{4}⁡\theta -{tan}^{2}⁡\theta }{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can further simplify our expression and use again $(2)$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{tan}^{4}⁡\theta -{tan}^{2}⁡\theta }{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta } & =\frac{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta ({tan}^{2}⁡\theta -1)}{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\cancel{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta }({tan}^{2}⁡\theta -1)}{\cancel{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta }} \\  & ={tan}^{2}⁡\theta -1 \\  & =({sec}^{2}⁡\theta -1)-1 \\  & ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta -2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{{tan}^{4}⁡\theta -{sec}^{2}⁡\theta +1}{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta }={sec}^{2}⁡\theta -2.
$$

after.name: Question 15
after.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${sec}^{4}⁡x-2{sec}^{2}⁡x+1+{tan}^{2}⁡x?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

$$
\begin{aligned} & (1) & 1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x \\  & (2) & {tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x-1 \\  & (3) & {sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x=1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can rewrite our expression using $(2),$ as follows:

$$
{sec}^{4}⁡x-2{sec}^{2}⁡x+1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{4}⁡x-2{sec}^{2}⁡x+1+{sec}^{2}⁡x-1
$$

Next, we can further simplify our expression and use again $(2),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{sec}^{4}⁡x-2{sec}^{2}⁡x+1+{sec}^{2}⁡x-1 & ={sec}^{4}⁡x-2{sec}^{2}⁡x+\cancel{1}+{sec}^{2}⁡x-\cancel{1} \\  & ={sec}^{4}⁡x-{sec}^{2}⁡x \\  & ={sec}^{2}⁡x\cdot ({sec}^{2}⁡x-1) \\  & ={sec}^{2}⁡x\cdot {tan}^{2}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
{sec}^{4}⁡x-2{sec}^{2}⁡x+1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x{tan}^{2}⁡x.

Question 15
?

Which of the following is equivalent to sec4⁡x−2sec2⁡x+1+tan2⁡x?

a
sec2⁡xtan⁡x
b
sec2⁡xtan4⁡x
c
sec4⁡xtan2⁡x
d
sec⁡xtan2⁡x
e
sec2⁡xtan2⁡x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

(1)1+tan2⁡x=sec2⁡x(2)tan2⁡x=sec2⁡x−1(3)sec2⁡x−tan2⁡x=1

Therefore, we can rewrite our expression using (2), as follows: sec4⁡x−2sec2⁡x+1+tan2⁡x=sec4⁡x−2sec2⁡x+1+sec2⁡x−1

Next, we can further simplify our expression and use again (2), as follows:

sec4⁡x−2sec2⁡x+1+sec2⁡x−1=sec4⁡x−2sec2⁡x+1+sec2⁡x−1=sec4⁡x−sec2⁡x=sec2⁡x⋅(sec2⁡x−1)=sec2⁡x⋅tan2⁡x

Therefore, we conclude that

sec4⁡x−2sec2⁡x+1+tan2⁡x=sec2⁡xtan2⁡x.

content.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${sec}^{4}⁡x-2{sec}^{2}⁡x+1+{tan}^{2}⁡x?$
content.worked_solution:
First, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

$$
\begin{aligned} & (1) & 1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x \\  & (2) & {tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x-1 \\  & (3) & {sec}^{2}⁡x-{tan}^{2}⁡x=1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can rewrite our expression using $(2),$ as follows:

$$
{sec}^{4}⁡x-2{sec}^{2}⁡x+1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{4}⁡x-2{sec}^{2}⁡x+1+{sec}^{2}⁡x-1
$$

Next, we can further simplify our expression and use again $(2),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{sec}^{4}⁡x-2{sec}^{2}⁡x+1+{sec}^{2}⁡x-1 & ={sec}^{4}⁡x-2{sec}^{2}⁡x+\cancel{1}+{sec}^{2}⁡x-\cancel{1} \\  & ={sec}^{4}⁡x-{sec}^{2}⁡x \\  & ={sec}^{2}⁡x\cdot ({sec}^{2}⁡x-1) \\  & ={sec}^{2}⁡x\cdot {tan}^{2}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
{sec}^{4}⁡x-2{sec}^{2}⁡x+1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x{tan}^{2}⁡x.
$$
